senses.definition: To the fullest extent or degree.
examples: They've totally demolished the bank on Main Street.

quotes.text:
Antonio. He misses not much.
Sebastian. No; he doth but mistake the truth totally.
quotes.reference: 1610–1611 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The Tempest”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London: […] Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act II, scene i]:

quotes.text: The languages of different nations did not totally differ […] They were therefore easily learned;
quotes.reference: 1789, Olaudah Equiano, chapter 2, in The Interesting Narrative of the Life of Olaudah Equiano, volume 1, London: for the author, page 59:

quotes.text: Your conjecture is totally wrong, I assure you.
